title: MIRO: MultI-Reward cOnditioned pretraining improves T2I quality and efficiency
claim: Our model produces diverse, high-quality, prompt-faithful images across styles and subjects, showing the quality of its samples.
layout: 3 rows mosaic gallery, 4 large images on top, 8 smaller each below
description: A dense mosaic of generated images with no text, arrows or axes. The top row has four large square images: an erupting volcano, a colorful painted portrait of a woman, a photorealistic portrait of a dark-skinned woman, and a giant banded planet over mountains. The second and third rows each hold eight smaller images. They include an astronaut by a pyramid, two rabbits in suits, a dog in a beanie, a storefront, a pharaoh, an octopus reading a book, fireworks over a city, sunflowers in a vase, a giant wave, a kitchen, latte art reading 'LOVE' and 'PEACE', a ship before the moon, a dragon and castle, a futuristic city, a pyramid, and an astronaut on horseback. The images cover photorealism, painting, fantasy and illustration. The eye goes first to the large top-row images.
caption: Images from our MIRO Synth model on PartiPrompt[ref].
abstract: The default paradigm of post-training text-to-image generators includes post-hoc selection of generated images, and subsequent training with one reward model to align the generator to the reward, typically user preference. This discards informative data as well as optimizes only for a single reward, hence harming diversity, semantic fidelity and efficiency. Instead, we propose MIRO, a method that conditions the model on multiple rewards during training, thus letting the model learn user preferences directly. MIRO pre-training both improves the visual quality of the generated images and speeds up the training, achieving state of the art on the GenEval compositional benchmark and user-preference scores (PickAScore, ImageReward, HPSv2).
